# The Last Legacy of the Smith Family: Coins, Spirits, and the Forgotten World of Wampong

By Drew Paul (ChatGPT)
April 24, 3025 | Wampong Times

In 3025, after the Collapse, the land of Wampong remains, home to the Smith family, the last heirs of a forgotten craft. Their legacy is tied to ancient coins, forged by the world’s first coin smiths, imbued with a strange power: they land on “heads” or “tails” with 80% accuracy, but only when spoken to near the ocean, with the spirits’ guidance.

On her 80th birthday, matriarch Luisa Smith XIV passed down these coins to her grandchildren, warning them to respect the old ways. However, the grandchildren were skeptical. While they knew not to openly question their grandmother’s instructions, they resolved to test the coins themselves.

As soon as they received them, they each retreated to their private bedrooms in the Smith family mansion. Thabo and Juan went upstairs to the second floor, where they slept in adjacent rooms. Marisol and Sarah went to the basement, each in opposite rooms. Without mentioning it to each other, they all began their tests, calling “heads” or “tails” and noting the results.

Thabo called “tails” 100 times, and 88 of the flips landed on tails. Juan, in the room next door, did the same with 84 out of 100 flips landing on tails. Downstairs, Marisol called “tails” consistently, but only 45 of her flips landed that way. Sarah, on the other hand, called “heads” every time, with only 53 out of 100 flips landing on heads.

The next morning, Thabo and Juan were eager to share their success. They were convinced the coins were real, and perhaps even more powerful than their grandmother had claimed. Marisol and Sarah, however, were dejected. Their coins had not worked as promised, and they couldn’t understand why.

When Luisa saw their faces, she knew immediately what had happened. She explained that the coins would only respond when spoken to in solitude, near the ocean, and with respect for the old rituals. Testing them in isolation, without following the proper ways, had angered the spirits and disrupted the magic.

For the Smith family, these coins are more than relics; they are links to a world before the Collapse. In a time where survival is paramount, they must decide: will they respect the old ways, or let the magic fade into myth?

In Wampong, where the ocean whispers, only the Smiths still remember the spirits’ call.
